advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Factor the container-needs-non-empty-`children` predicate into one shared helper used by both `provider_parity._runnable` and `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` (or have `_runnable` delegate), so eligibility cannot drift from actual runnability.
evidence: provider_parity.py:168-170 `if solver_id in CONTAINER_CRITERIA: children = case.get("children"); return isinstance(children, list) and bool(children)`
eval_solver.py:110-116 `if cid in CONTAINER_CRITERIA: children = case.get("children"); if not isinstance(children, list) or not children: raise ValueError(...)`
The two conditions are exact logical complements today but are maintained in separate modules with no shared helper or cross-reference, so a change to one is not enforced on the other.
advisory.finding: `_runnable` in provider_parity.py duplicates the container-needs-non-empty-`children` rule that `eval_solver._run_criterion_case` enforces independently; the two are not linked, so if the runtime rule changes (e.g. a container criterion gains an inline path, or `decomp-shape` learns to synthesize children) eligibility will silently diverge from actual runnability and a case can again land in the error counts instead of producing a verdict — the exact failure this guard exists to prevent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that a container-criterion case WITH a `children` payload (e.g. a decomp-shape case) remains present in `eligible_cases()` output, so over-exclusion regressions in `_runnable` are caught.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:168-171 applies the children-required rule to ALL container criteria, including decomp-shape

plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml:45 `children:` — decomp-shape (a container criterion) fixtures carry children and stay eligible; provider_parity_results.json:425 records DSHAPE cases in the scored corpus

ABSENCE: search of tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py for 'decomp-shape' returns no matches; the test only asserts `_runnable('G3', {'children': [...]})` in isolation (line 295), never that a real container case with children survives `eligible_cases()`
advisory.finding: The new test verifies the exclusion path (container cases without `children` are dropped) but never asserts, against real `eligible_cases()` output, that container-criterion cases WITH a `children` payload remain eligible. `decomp-shape` is a CONTAINER_CRITERIA member whose fixtures carry `children` and appear in the corpus; the only positive `_runnable` check is a synthetic dict, not the integrated selector path. A regression that over-excludes container criteria (e.g. dropping `bool(children)` and returning False, or inverting the children check) would silently remove legitimate decomp-shape corpus items while every current assertion still passes.
scenarios: A future refactor of `_runnable` that unconditionally excludes container criteria, or inverts the `bool(children)` guard, silently drops decomp-shape corpus items and shrinks the scored pair set without any test failing.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_container_cases_without_a_children_payload_are_excluded, add: `assert any(i.spec == 'plan-review-decomp-shape' for i in pp.eligible_cases())` (or assert some container-criterion item survives with a non-empty children payload), pairing the exclusion guard with an inclusion-preservation guard.
